description: Ground-truth corpus for Experiments 2.1 and 2.2 (embedder comparison; embedder x doc-text format). Each entry pairs a (food_description, field) with the food_properties.csv or food_pathogen_hazards.csv row(s) the production retrieval should return. The harness applies the same query reformulation and thresholds the production RetrievalService uses; the corpus does not hard-code reformulated query strings. Doc IDs are resolved by food_name lookup against the live ingestion pipeline at harness startup. NOTE — medium-stratum MRR is predominantly an aw-retrieval signal: only 2 of 20 medium queries test pH retrieval at the category level, reflecting the underlying scarcity of category-level pH data in food_properties.csv. Do not interpret medium-MRR as a balanced pH/aw signal.

schema.food_description: Input to GroundingService — the same string the production pipeline would pass to query_food_properties / query_food_ph / query_food_water_activity / query_pathogen_hazards
schema.field: Which production query type to invoke: 'ph' (Tier 2 pH fallback) | 'water_activity' (Tier 2 aw fallback) | 'ph_aw_combined' (Tier 1 primary, evaluates pH and aw on the same Tier 1 doc) | 'pathogen' (Pathogen Stage 1)
schema.production_tier: Which production retrieval tier this query exercises: 'tier_1' (food_properties_confidence=0.70) | 'tier_2' (food_properties_fallback_confidence=0.62) | 'pathogen_stage_1' (pathogen_hazards_confidence=0.75)
schema.tier: Difficulty stratum for analysis: 'easy' (specific-food row exists in food_properties) | 'medium' (category-level row exists in food_properties) | 'hard' (no doc exists at embedder layer — negative control or genuine miss) | 'pathogen' (food_pathogen_hazards row exists)
schema.acceptable_food_names: Ordered list of food_name values whose row would be a correct top-1 match. First element is canonical-best. Empty list means no doc should clear the threshold (negative control).
schema.expected_doc_text_hint: Human-readable text for verification; not consumed by the harness
schema.source: Provenance of this corpus entry (test_journal_QNN | species_probe | species_probe_negative | negative_control)
schema.comment: Why this query is in the corpus

queries.comment: Canonical Tier 1 specific-food match. The chicken row has pH but no aw, so Tier 2 aw fallback would fire downstream — out of scope for this entry, which tests Tier 1 only.
Conversational variant of E01. Tests that 'raw' prefix doesn't degrade the embedder's match to the chicken row.

queries.expected_doc_text_hint: bread white (grain): pH 5.0 to 6.2, aw 0.94 to 0.97
queries.comment: Specific food with BOTH pH and aw and two source IDs (FDA-PH-2007 + IFT-2003-T31). Canonical Tier 1 dual-field case.
Tests word-order tolerance — query is 'ground beef' but row is 'beef ground'.
Single-token specific-food row.
Common name 'milk' should match 'milk cow' as the canonical whole-cow-milk row.
Specific-fish row exists. Tests fish vocabulary.
Word-order tolerance — query is 'canned tuna', row is 'tuna fish canned'.
Shellfish category direct match.

Composite-keyword test — 'cooked' and 'rice' are not composite-food triggers (soup/chili/stew/lasagna are), so retrieval should fire. If the composite-food guard wrongly skips this, the harness should flag it.

queries.expected_doc_text_hint: cheese parmesan (dairy): pH 5.2 to 5.3. water activity 0.68 to 0.76
queries.comment: One of only three food_properties.csv rows with BOTH pH and aw populated (excluding bread white, already E03). Tests word-order tolerance — query 'parmesan cheese' vs row 'cheese parmesan'. Hard aged cheese with low aw is a dual-field Tier 1 test spanning different preservation mechanisms from bread white.

Dairy row with pH only. Tests qualifier tolerance — 'plain yogurt' vs row 'yogurt'. pH below 4.5 means this is near the safety boundary for most pathogens; an important anchor for the acid dairy region of the food space.

Grain row with pH only. Tests word-order tolerance — query 'rye bread' vs row 'bread rye'. Follows the same pattern as E04 (ground beef/beef ground) and E08 (canned tuna/tuna fish canned). Second grain entry after bread white (E03).

Grain row with pH only. Tests word-order tolerance — 'cooked oatmeal' vs row 'oatmeal cooked'. Near-neutral pH cooked grain; common in temperature-abuse scenarios. Analogous to E10 (cooked white rice / rice white cooked).

Fruit row with pH only. Tests qualifier tolerance — 'fresh strawberries' vs row 'strawberries'. Very low pH (below 4.0) — most pathogens cannot grow; tests that low-acid fruits are retrievable. First fruit entry in the corpus.

Vegetable row with pH only. Tests qualifier tolerance — 'fresh carrots' vs row 'carrots'. Near-neutral pH vegetable above the 4.6 safety threshold; first vegetable entry in the corpus. Analogous qualifier pattern to E07 (fresh salmon / salmon fresh).

One of only three food_properties.csv rows with BOTH pH and aw populated. Exact food_name match. Very low aw (0.75) inhibits microbial growth despite near-safety-boundary pH — tests dual-field retrieval for a water-activity-preserved product. Different aw range from bread white (0.94-0.97).

One of only three food_properties.csv rows with BOTH pH and aw populated. Exact food_name match. Mid-range aw (0.85) with near-neutral pH — tests dual-field retrieval for a moderately preserved product. Third dual-field entry alongside bread white (E03) and cheese parmesan (E11).
Species probe — no turkey-specific row exists. Canonical answer is the category-level fresh poultry row. Tier 2 aw fallback (query suffix 'water activity aw moisture') should hit at 0.62 threshold.
Species probe — same pattern as turkey.
Species probe — less-common poultry species.
Species probe — game poultry.
Species probe — no lamb-specific row. Canonical answer is the fresh meat category row.
Species probe — no pork-specific row. FoodEx2 aliases pork→pig (out of embedder scope; Tier 3 only).
Bare 'beef' (not 'beef ground'). FoodEx2 aliases beef→bovine (Tier 3 only). Tier 2 should hit fresh meat.
Note: 'eggs' is the category-level row with aw only. 'eggs whole new laid' has pH only. Tier 2 aw query should match 'eggs' not 'eggs whole new laid'.
Tests state-aware matching — cured vs fresh meat have very different aw ranges. The 'ham' specific row has pH only. Tier 2 aw should hit cured meat, not fresh meat.

queries.expected_doc_text_hint: codfish boiled (fish): pH 5.3 to 6.1 — OR — fish fresh most (fish): pH 6.6 to 6.8
queries.comment: Acceptable-list test — bare 'cod' could match 'codfish boiled' (specific) or 'fish fresh most' (category). Either is correct; codfish boiled is canonical. Tests the acceptable-list mechanism.

Species probe — no quail-specific row in food_properties.csv. Canonical answer is the category-level fresh poultry row (aw 0.99-1.0). Tier 2 aw fallback query 'quail water activity aw moisture' at 0.62 threshold. Note: quail pH would be hard stratum — no poultry-pH category row exists. Adds a fifth poultry species to M01-M04 (turkey, duck, goose, pheasant).

Species probe — no guinea fowl row in food_properties.csv. Less-common poultry species (Numida meleagris) tests category generalisation beyond the turkey/duck/goose/pheasant cluster already in corpus. Same pattern as M01-M04.

Species probe — no venison (deer meat) row in food_properties.csv. Game meat that maps to the fresh meat category for aw. Same pattern as M05 (lamb) and M06 (pork). Tests that the embedder generalises game mammals to the fresh meat category.

Species probe — no bison row in food_properties.csv. North American large ungulate; increasingly common in food service. Tests fresh meat category generalisation beyond the common European livestock species (lamb, pork, beef) already in corpus.

Species probe — no pepperoni row in food_properties.csv. Dry-cured fermented sausage; aw typically 0.85-0.90 which is within the cured meat category range (0.87-0.95). Existing M09 covers cured ham; pepperoni adds a processed/emulsified cured product. Tests whether the embedder maps processed cured sausages to the cured meat category.

Species probe — no salami row in food_properties.csv. Italian dry-cured fermented sausage; different vocabulary from pepperoni. Tests cross-product generalisation within cured processed meats. Together with M15, gives two independent tests of the cured-sausage → cured meat mapping.

Species probe — no halibut row in food_properties.csv. Flatfish; canonical answer is the fish fresh most category row (pH 6.6-6.8). Existing M10 (cod) has an acceptable specific row (codfish boiled); halibut does not — making this a purer category-only test. Tier 2 pH query 'halibut pH acidity' at 0.62 threshold.

Species probe — no tilapia row in food_properties.csv. Common farmed freshwater fish; widely used in food service. Tests whether the embedder generalises a freshwater farmed species to the 'fish fresh most' category. Second fish-pH medium entry alongside M10 (cod) and M17 (halibut).

Species probe — no quail eggs row in food_properties.csv. The category-level 'eggs' row provides aw 0.97. Note: 'eggs whole new laid' has pH only; for aw the only row is the category 'eggs'. Query 'quail eggs water activity aw moisture' at 0.62 threshold. Tests egg-species generalisation.

Species probe — no duck eggs row in food_properties.csv. Less-common egg type; used in baking and Asian cuisine. Tests whether 'duck eggs' maps to the generic 'eggs' category row at the Tier 2 aw threshold. Together with M19 gives two distinct non-chicken egg species for the eggs category.

Genuine no-doc-at-embedder-layer case. No turkey pH row exists in food_properties.csv; no poultry-pH category row exists either. Correct behaviour: no doc clears the 0.62 threshold. In production, Tier 3 (FoodEx2 bridge) handles this. For the embedder benchmark, 'no match above threshold' is the correct answer; the metric should reward not over-matching.
Same pattern as H01. No poultry pH at embedder layer.
No lamb-specific row, no meat-category pH row in food_properties.csv. 'fresh meat' (line 28) has aw only, no pH.
No pork pH at embedder layer.

Made-up food. Correct behaviour: no doc clears the 0.62 threshold. Tests that the embedder does not over-match nonsense input. Bad embedders may match 'burger'-adjacent rows (e.g., ground beef) with spurious confidence.
Made-up food, aw query variant. Same pattern as H05.

Made-up food with a plausible real-food suffix ('steak'). Correct behaviour: no doc clears the 0.62 threshold. Tests whether the real token 'steak' anchors to beef/meat rows with spurious high confidence. Bad embedders may over-match the 'steak' semantic cluster. Mirrors H05/H06 pattern with a different surface form.

Made-up food with a semantically neutral suffix ('bar'). Correct behaviour: no doc clears the 0.62 threshold for the aw query. 'Bar' does not strongly anchor to any food category in the KB. Tests general non-match robustness for an aw query, complementing H07 (pH query).

Real food absent from KB at embedder layer for pH. No rabbit row in food_properties.csv. The fresh meat category row exists but has aw only — no pH data. So no valid row exists for a pH query. In production, Tier 3 (FoodEx2 bridge) would handle this. For the embedder benchmark, no doc clearing 0.62 is the correct outcome. Analogous to H01-H04 (poultry species, pH).

Real food absent from KB at embedder layer for pH. No ostrich row in food_properties.csv. The fresh poultry category row exists but has aw only — no pH. Ratite bird; commercially farmed in South Africa and increasingly globally. Adds a structurally identical hard case to H01 (turkey pH) and H02 (duck pH) using a more exotic species that bad embedders are less likely to have seen paired with poultry category terms.

Unqualified generic class noun — no species, state, or preparation qualifier. Correct behaviour: no doc clears 0.62. Meat-specific pH rows exist (beef ground, ham, veal) but grounding pH on a bare generic-class query is epistemically wrong; the system should seek clarification. Bad embedders may match 'beef ground' or 'ham' above threshold. Tests over-specificity resistance on unqualified class terms. Ambiguous generic — no defensible category match exists because multiple specific-food rows compete on shared tokens. Correct behaviour is no doc above threshold; a high-scoring match indicates over-confidence on tokens shared across the category. Placed in hard (not medium) because there is no canonical-best answer.

Unqualified generic class noun for aw. A 'fresh fish' aw category row exists (0.99-1.0) but grounding aw on bare 'fish' is wrong: fresh, smoked, and canned fish have radically different aw (0.99, 0.96, 0.80 respectively). The system should not match. Bad embedders may retrieve 'fresh fish' above 0.62. Mirrors H11 pattern for a different field and food class. Ambiguous generic — no defensible category match exists because multiple specific-food rows compete on shared tokens. Correct behaviour is no doc above threshold; a high-scoring match indicates over-confidence on tokens shared across the category. Placed in hard (not medium) because there is no canonical-best answer.

queries.expected_doc_text_hint: Hazard for chicken raw: Salmonella spp. (annual_deaths_us=238)
queries.comment: Pathogen Stage 1 — query suffix 'food hazard', threshold 0.75. Stage 1 resolves food name; Stage 2 (metadata filter, no embedder) selects pathogen by annual_deaths_us. Embedder benchmark covers Stage 1 only.

queries.expected_doc_text_hint: Hazard for beef raw: E. coli O157:H7
queries.comment: Word-order — query 'raw beef', row 'beef raw'.

queries.expected_doc_text_hint: Hazard for oysters raw: Vibrio vulnificus (CFR 35%)
queries.comment: Shellfish pathogen retrieval.

queries.expected_doc_text_hint: Hazard for salmon raw: Listeria monocytogenes
queries.comment: Fish pathogen retrieval.

queries.expected_doc_text_hint: Hazard for shrimp raw: Vibrio parahaemolyticus (primary hazard). Stage 2 top-ranked by deaths: Salmonella spp. (238)
queries.comment: Shellfish pathogen retrieval. Stage 1 should retrieve shrimp raw hazard docs above 0.75 threshold for 'raw shrimp food hazard'. Word-order variant: 'raw shrimp' vs row 'shrimp raw'. Stage 2 (out of scope) would rank: Salmonella 238 > Listeria 172 > Vibrio 4 by annual_deaths_us.

queries.expected_doc_text_hint: Hazard for pork raw: Salmonella spp. (primary hazard, 238 annual US deaths)
queries.comment: Meat pathogen retrieval. Word-order variant: 'raw pork' vs row 'pork raw'. Stage 2 ranking: Salmonella 238 > Listeria 172 > Yersinia 29 > Trichinella 0. Yersinia enterocolitica is a distinctive pork-associated pathogen (primary_hazard=yes) not present in beef or poultry categories — diagnostically valuable.

queries.expected_doc_text_hint: Hazard for rice cooked: Bacillus cereus (primary_hazard=yes, emetic toxin). Stage 2 top-ranked by deaths: Clostridium perfringens (41)
queries.comment: Grain pathogen retrieval. Tests that 'cooked rice food hazard' retrieves 'rice cooked' hazard docs at 0.75 threshold. Tension in data: B. cereus is primary_hazard=yes but annual_deaths_us=0; C. perfringens is primary_hazard=no but annual_deaths_us=41. Stage 2 would select C. perfringens by deaths. Both are real spore-forming concerns for cooked rice held at room temperature. Embedder evaluation only — Stage 1 food-name resolution. The Stage 2 pathogen selection (deterministic, by annual_deaths_us) would pick C. perfringens regardless of which embedder runs Stage 1. B. cereus is the primary_hazard flag in the CSV but with 0 deaths it is not what production returns.

queries.expected_doc_text_hint: Hazard for lettuce raw: Escherichia coli O157:H7 (primary hazard, 40 annual US deaths)
queries.comment: Produce pathogen retrieval. Vocabulary variant: 'fresh lettuce' vs row 'lettuce raw'. Tests whether the pathogen-stage-1 query bridges the 'fresh' descriptor to the 'raw' food_name at 0.75 threshold. E. coli O157:H7 is the primary pathogen of concern for leafy greens (2006 major outbreak source).

queries.expected_doc_text_hint: Hazard for eggs raw: Salmonella Enteritidis (primary hazard, vertical transmission)
queries.comment: Egg pathogen retrieval. Word-order variant: 'raw eggs' vs row 'eggs raw'. Salmonella Enteritidis (annual_deaths_us=238) is the defining pathogen for raw egg scenarios via vertical (transovarian) transmission. Stage 2 ranking: Salmonella Enteritidis 238 > Listeria monocytogenes 172.

queries.expected_doc_text_hint: Hazard for milk raw unpasteurized: Listeria monocytogenes (primary hazard, 15-30% case fatality rate)
queries.comment: Dairy pathogen retrieval. Vocabulary variant: 'raw milk' (consumer term) vs row 'milk raw unpasteurized' (regulatory term). Tests that stage-1 query bridges the abbreviated common term to the longer food_name at 0.75 threshold. Stage 2 ranking by deaths: Salmonella 238 > Campylobacter 197 > Listeria 172 > E. coli 40 — note Listeria is primary_hazard=yes despite ranking 3rd by deaths.

metric_notes.correct_at_1: For non-empty acceptable_food_names, the embedder's top-1 doc above the relevant threshold must be in the acceptable_food_names list. For empty acceptable_food_names (negative controls), correct@1 is True if NO doc clears the threshold.
metric_notes.expected_score: For non-empty acceptable_food_names: cosine similarity of the canonical (first) acceptable food's doc. Null if not in top-K. For negative controls: not applicable (report null or the highest doc's score for diagnostic purposes).
metric_notes.gate_pass_rate: For positive cases: did the canonical doc clear the production threshold (0.62 / 0.70 / 0.75 depending on field). For negative controls: did NO doc clear the threshold.
metric_notes.stratified_accuracy: Report top-1 accuracy and gate-pass-rate separately per stratum. The decision chart should highlight the medium stratum (species probes) since that is the failure mode motivating this experiment.
metric_notes.medium_stratum_composition: 8 of 20 medium queries target fresh poultry (M01-M04, M11-M12) or fresh meat (M05-M07, M13-M14) aw; 4 target cured meat (M09, M15-M16) or eggs (M08, M19-M20) aw; 2 target eggs aw (M19, M20); only 4 target pH (M10, M17, M18) or any non-aw field. Do not interpret medium-MRR as a balanced pH/aw signal.
